transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (NovaSearch Head of Search), Ben Liu (ML Eng), Carlos Mendes (PM)

Summary:
Short demo of Redwood Hosted API focusing on embeddings + rerank flows for improving NovaSearch relevance. Showed console snippets, API curl examples, and Optimize suggestions for cost/latency tuning. Discussed pilot plan and next steps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh i'm maya from redwood, with luis our se - quick intro, can you each say hi and role?
[00:06] Aisha: hey i'm aisha, head of search at novasearch, we own ranking and infra for web results, excited to see how embeddings + rerank can help long tail queries
[00:12] Ben: ben here, ml eng, mostly infra and evaluation pipelines
[00:15] Carlos: carlos, product, i'll be owning success criteria for pilot
[00:18] Luis: thanks, luis here, i'll walk through the technical demo and the rerank call path today

[02:05] Maya: quick agenda, one: overview of hosted api for embeddings and rerank, two: demo live console + curl, three: talk about Optimize recs and costs, four: pilot next steps/Q&A

[04:20] Luis: ok show of the console - you can see model catalog, we're using the redwood-embed-1024-ish family in this demo (note: model names in dev changes), embeddings endpoint returns 1024 vectors by default, you can choose 512 as well for smaller token costs
[04:47] Ben: what's the latency ballpark for embedding calls, p95 for 512 vectors?
[04:52] Luis: on hosted, typical p95 is 30-80ms for single doc embed depending on model and batching; for our demo dataset with batch size 16 we saw ~120ms per batch; single-sync calls are sub-100ms often, but depends on sequence length

[07:15] Aisha: ok for search we care about query latency - our frontend needs <200ms for query turnaround ideally. Does rerank add a lot?
[07:23] Luis: rerank is a second-stage scoring call - flow we recommend: ANN recall -> topN (e.g., 100) -> rerank with the rerank endpoint. Rerank p95 for top 100 with redwood-hosted quantized models is often 120-300ms depending on model and context length. Combined with ANN retrieval it's possible to be under your 200-300ms SLA if tuned. We also showed caching options (prefix/KV cache) to speed repeated queries

[09:40] Carlos: are there cost tradeoffs? like embeddings per doc + rerank per candidate - can you quantify?
[09:47] Maya: yeah good Q - cost factors: vector dimension / model size, number of candidates for rerank, how much batching you can do on the server side. we'll send a cost spreadsheet but rough: embeddings per doc small (couple of microcents) but reranking 100 candidates per query is the bigger driver. Optimize suggests caching embeddings for static docs and only reranking top 20 by default to save cost

[12:02] Ben: how much does batching help - if we batch 32 queries for embeddings, does p95 improve?
[12:08] Luis: batching increases throughput and lowers per-unit cost but can add latency for the first requester; continuous batching with small time windows helps. For embedded service, batching gave us ~3-4x throughput gains in our benchmarks. Optimize can recommend batch sizes based on your query distribution

[15:30] Maya: quick note on security - hosted has SOC 2, SSO via SAML/OAuth, customer KMS support for encryption at rest and contractable retention windows, we can share security pack after this call
[15:47] Aisha: we need SOC 2 report + architecture diagram and to know if logs include customer PII - we generally scrub logs before sharing but want assurance
[15:55] Maya: yes we'll send the security pack including SOC 2, dataflow, and audit log details. logs are access-controlled, retention configurable

[19:10] Luis: demo time - i'm going to do a 2-stage example: index a few docs, run ANN recall via open-source index (we used milvus in the demo), then call the Redwood rerank endpoint. showing curl: POST /v1/embeddings -> returns base64-ish vector array POST /v1/search/rerank -> body includes query, candidates (ids + text), model param and return ranked ids with scores

[21:40] Luis: note on API params: temperature etc don't apply to rerank, it's deterministic scoring; you can pass metadata for explainability. Also we have a batch rerank endpoint if you want to rerank multiple queries in one call - that reduces API overhead

[24:50] Ben: in your example the rerank uses cross-encoder style scoring? how big is the context window?
[24:55] Luis: yes, cross-attention between query and candidate; context window needs to fit query+candidate length - for long docs we use candidate sharding or truncated passages. We also support handy heuristics like scoring on passage rather than whole doc to stay in window

[28:00] Aisha: curious about quality - do you have automated evals or zero-shot vs fine-tuned models?
[28:10] Luis: we ship with curated open models and have in-platform eval harness - you can upload labeled relevance sets and run batch evals, get MRR/ndcg comparisons. Redwood Optimize can recommend model variants and quantization level if you want to trade slight accuracy for cost. We recommended a pilot with host-model A then compare host-model B quantized to see regression

[31:20] Carlos: for pilot what's realistic scope? two weeks? 100k queries?
[31:28] Maya: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks, pick a slice of logs (50k-200k queries) and we can run A/B via routing, or run batch offline evals first. we usually do hosted to start, then move to dedicated if you need predictable throughput or data isolation

[34:05] Ben: any red flags with our infra - we use GCP, have VPC peering requirements and strict SSO enforcement
[34:12] Maya: hosted supports private networking via VPC connectors for enterprise or you can deploy Redwood Private. For SSO/SAML we support SCIM provisioning and RBAC. we'll include network diagrams and options

[36:50] Luis: now a short live rerank example - sending three queries, showing candidate scores, pointing out when rerank flips order relative to ANN. you'll notice some transcriptions in the console logs are truncated, that's dev console artifact not data loss

[40:15] Aisha: good, i liked the explainability metadata. can you expose why an item scored higher?
[40:20] Luis: we provide score breakdowns per token span on request and explainability tags. not full attention weights but helpful heuristics: similarity score, context overlap, penalize length mismatch. we can surface top tokens that influenced score

[43:30] Carlos: question on SLOs - what uptime and latency guarantees for hosted?
[43:34] Maya: hosted has best-effort SLAs; dedicated gets SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers. if you require 99.95% w/ latency targets we recommend Dedicated or hybrid routing with fallbacks. we'll outline options in the pricing doc

[46:50] Ben: any examples of customers who moved from embeddings-only to rerank and saw big lifts?
[46:55] Maya: yes, we've seen several search customers get +8-15% MRR improvement on tail queries after rerank tuning; we'll share anonymized case studies in the follow-up pack

[48:20] Aisha: ok next steps, we need pricing, security documents, and a quick benchmark from you. can you run a quick 1k query rerank with our sample format?
[48:33] Luis: yes i'll run that - please share a small anonymized slice of logs, we'll run the 1k and return p50/p95 latency and token cost breakdown

[50:05] Maya: recap: maya send pricing + security pack by Aug 5, luis run rerank bench by Aug 10, aisha share logs + confirm pilot scope by Aug 6, schedule 30 min pilot kickoff week of Aug 16. Any other open Qs?
[50:30] Carlos: none from me, thanks all
[50:35] Ben: all good
[50:40] Aisha: great thanks, talk soon

[51:00] End meeting
